finalJustifications: Because the customised policy applies the least privilege in both axes: only the necessary actions (Put/Get/List) and only the RECURSO necessary (or ARN Builds Bucket).
Because the custom policy inherits the permissions of AmazonS3FullAccess and filters them in runtime by the pocket accessed on the call.
Because custom policy automatically expires at the end of each build, reducing the credentials display window.
Because custom policy records every upload in CloudTrail with prior approval, the control required by compliance.

optionReasons.saa-med-162:option:0: A single SG with freed internal traffic flats the layers — any committed instance reaches the bank.
optionReasons.saa-med-162:option:1: NACLs are statesss and by sub-network — complement, but do not replace the fine control by origin that the requirement asks.
optionReasons.saa-med-162:option:3: It's the closest because it's a real rule of Security Group which 'works' — but allows the CIDR of VPC INTEIRA: the web layer (and any network resource) would reach the bank directly; the ID string of Security Group restricts to layer immediately before.

finalJustifications: Because chaining by SG ID implements the defense in depth: the bank only accepts origin in the application's SG, and the application only the SG of the ALB — layer to layer, no IPs.
Because the SG chain creates encrypted tunnels between the layers of the application, isolating the internal traffic of the rest of the VPC.
Because referring SGs makes the rules inherit the IPs of NACLs of the sub-networks involved, unifying the two layers of firewall.
Because the SG of RDS block by default the web layer when detecting the ALB in the chain, applying layer topology automatically.

optionReasons.saa-med-164:option:0: Changing the storage class does not add any verification — Deep Archive is cost, not exclusion control.
optionReasons.saa-med-164:option:1: Encryption protects content reading — encrypted objects can normally be deleted by those who have permission.
optionReasons.saa-med-164:option:3: It's the closest one to deny it. s3:DeleteObject by policy in fact prevents exclusions — but anyone who compromises credentials with the power to edit the policy removes the protection together; the layer ADICIONAL requested (MFA at the time of the request) is the MFA Delete with versioning.

finalJustifications: Because MFA Delete with versioning requires a code MFA valid in the application itself to exclude versions permanently — stolen credentials without token destroys nothing.
Because MFA Delete encrypts old versions with a token derived key MFA, making them unreadable without the physical device.
Because MFA Delete transfers the exclusions to an approval row of 24 hours, all reversible by the administrator within that time limit.
Because MFA Delete blocks user after three exclusion attempts without token, freezing compromised credentials at time.

optionReasons.saa-med-167:option:0: It's the closest because Storage Lens also analyzes bucket activity — but in metrics AGREGADAS (volume, total requests); it does not record individual calls with identity and IP: API by caller is the CloudTrail (with data events for GetObject).
optionReasons.saa-med-167:option:2: The Trusted Advisor recommends good practices — does not record transactions in access to newsletters.
optionReasons.saa-med-167:option:3: The CloudWatch Logs does not store logs of API of the S3 'by default' — receives only what is explicitly configured.

finalJustifications: Because CloudTrail records calls from API with identity, timestamp and IP of origin — and data events enabled, it covers GetObject/PutObject/DeleteObject by pocket.
Because CloudTrail records captures of user console sessions, visually revealing who sailed through the investigated pocket.
Because CloudTrail intercepts suspicious calls in real time and blocks them before the object is read by the external invader.
Because CloudTrail rebuilds the 90 days of history retroactively from the access metadata of the objects of the bucket.

optionReasons.saa-med-168:option:0: The Trusted Advisor in the basic plan only brings a minimum subset of checks — complete checks require Business/Enterprise, and yet no history of compliance by resource.
optionReasons.saa-med-168:option:1: It's the closest because the Lambda Scheduled FUNCIONARIA — but it is its own code to maintain, it rotates in windows (not continuously) and does not generate history of conformity; the AWS Config delivers ready rules, continuous evaluation and compliance trail by resource.
optionReasons.saa-med-168:option:3: The Inspector search CVEs and network exposure in instances and images — does not evaluate volume encryption or SG rule against policy.

finalJustifications: Because Config with encrypted-volumes and restricted-ssh rules continuously evaluates every creation and change, notify violations and maintain the compliance history.
Because Config fixes violations automatically by default, encrypting the volumes and closing the door 22 without approval.
Because Config prevents the creation of resources outside of politics, canceling the call of API before the appeal exists in the account.
Because Config delegates the evaluation to Trusted Advisor and consolidates the results into a single account compliance panel.

optionReasons.saa-med-169:option:0: X-Ray tracks requests within the APPLICATION (trace) — does not capture IP traffic from network interfaces.

optionReasons.saa-med-169:option:2: It's the closest because the log accesses of ALB they also record real traffic — but only what goes through the balancer: direct connections of the instances with external destinations (suspicious traffic) do not even appear; TODO the traffic of the ENIs are the VPC Flow Logs.

finalJustifications: Because the VPC Flow Logs capture metadata from all ENI traffic — origin, destination, ports, bytes and ACCEPT/REJECT — delivered to CloudWatch or S3.
Because the VPC Flow Logs also record the payload of rejected connections, allowing you to reproduce the attack in the laboratory.
Because the VPC Flow Logs block known malicious destinations automatically while recording the rest of traffic.
Because the VPC Flow Logs consult the Security Group and note which rule approved each flow, pointing to the explored gap.

optionReasons.saa-med-170:option:0: Excluding and re-creating objects annually is mass reprocessing disguised — exactly what you want to avoid.
optionReasons.saa-med-170:option:2: It's the closest because creating new keys periodically It's a valid form of rotation — but it requires updating every pocket and volume for the new Key ID and managing the old key for historical data; automatic rotation does this internally by maintaining the same ARN.
optionReasons.saa-med-170:option:3: Disabling encryption to re-encrypt exposes data in the interval — risk operation without need.

finalJustifications: Because automatic rotation exchanges cryptographic material annually maintaining the MESMO Key ID/ARN — o KMS saves old versions and deciphers historical data alone.
Because automatic rotation re-encrypts existing background data, updating objects without maintenance window.
Because automatic rotation emits a new ARN per year and updates the references in the services via Parameter Store integrated.
Because automatic rotation divides the key into independent versions by resource, and each pocket uses the one of its original creation.
